programs.label: Programs
programs.title: From kindergarten to TOEFL-ready.
programs.lead: Each level runs for {months} months. No need to guess where to start — the free placement test decides.
programs.note: not sure which level? that’s what the free test is for

kindergarten.summary: Songs, movement and picture stories. Meeting English without the fear.
kindergarten.overview1: At this age the goal is simple: your child should enjoy English first. We learn through songs, movement, pictures and games — not long worksheets.
kindergarten.overview2: Classes cap at {count} children, so the teacher can greet each one and make sure the shy ones get a voice too.
kindergarten.level1: Greetings, colours, numbers and everyday objects. Answering with a single word.
kindergarten.level2: Simple action words and longer songs. Answering with two or three words.
kindergarten.level3: Short picture stories and first sentences. Ready for Standard.
kindergarten.fit1: Your child is in kindergarten and new to English.
kindergarten.fit2: They love singing and moving, but are shy to speak.
kindergarten.fit3: You want a fun start, not memorisation.
kindergarten.next: After Kindergarten 3, move up to Standard.

standard.summary: From single words to full sentences. Starting to answer the teacher out loud.
standard.overview1: Standard is for children in grades 1–3. Vocabulary turns into sentences, and children start reading simple English words.
standard.overview2: Every session still has speaking time. Teachers get children used to answering in full sentences — slowly, and nobody gets told off for mistakes.
standard.level1: Short sentences about themselves, their family and school.
standard.level2: Reading simple words and sentences. Asking and answering short questions.
standard.level3: Short talks about daily routines. Ready for Primary.
standard.fit2: They know some words but don’t dare build sentences yet.
standard.fit3: You want English at school to feel easier.
standard.next: After Standard 3, move up to Primary.

primary.summary: Reading short stories, retelling them, and chatting about their own day.
primary.overview1: Primary is for children in grades 4–6. They read longer texts, write short paragraphs and retell stories in their own words.
primary.overview2: Grammar comes in, but always through examples they actually say out loud. The aim: understanding why a sentence is right, not memorising formulas.
primary.level1: Reading short stories and answering questions about them.
primary.level2: Retelling stories and their own experiences out loud.
primary.level3: Writing short paragraphs and giving small presentations to the class. Ready for Elementary.
primary.fit2: Their grades are fine, but they freeze in conversation.
primary.fit3: You want a solid base before junior high.
primary.next: After Primary 3, move up to Elementary.

elementary.summary: Grammar foundations you use when speaking, not just memorise for tests.
elementary.overview1: Elementary is for junior high students and adults starting from the basics. We tidy up the foundations: the tenses you use most, everyday vocabulary, and how to ask questions.
elementary.overview2: Every grammar point goes straight into conversation in class. Mistakes get fixed together — nobody laughs.
elementary.level1: Basic sentences and everyday tenses. Introducing yourself with confidence.
elementary.level2: Talking about the past and future plans. Reading short texts.
elementary.level3: Short discussions and writing simple messages or emails. Ready for Intermediate.
elementary.fit1: You’re in junior high, or an adult starting from scratch.
elementary.fit2: You studied English at school for years but still fear speaking.
elementary.fit3: You need tidy foundations before moving up.
elementary.next: After Elementary 3, move up to Intermediate.

intermediate.summary: Discussions, presentations and tidy writing. Getting comfortable using English every day.
intermediate.overview1: Intermediate is for high school students, university students and working adults who already have the basics. The focus shifts from “correct” to “fluent”: discussions, presentations and clear writing.
intermediate.overview2: Classes run from late afternoon into the evening, so you can still make it after school, lectures or work.
intermediate.level1: Discussing everyday topics and giving opinions with reasons.
intermediate.level3: Light debates, summarising what you read, and speaking more spontaneously. Ready for Pre-TOEFL.
intermediate.fit1: You can read English, but your sentences stall when you speak.
intermediate.fit2: You need English for university or work.
intermediate.fit3: You want more confidence in presentations and meetings.
intermediate.next: After Intermediate 3, move on to Pre-TOEFL — or stop here if you’ve reached your goal.

pre-toefl.summary: Learn the TOEFL format, practise each section and plan your timing before the real test.
pre-toefl.overview1: Pre-TOEFL is for university students and professionals preparing for the TOEFL — for graduation, scholarships or work.
pre-toefl.overview2: We break down the test format, practise every section and drill your timing. This program is preparation; to register for an official TOEFL test, ask us on WhatsApp.
pre-toefl.level1: Listening Comprehension — following conversations and short talks.
pre-toefl.level2: Structure & Written Expression — the grammar patterns that come up most.
pre-toefl.level3: Reading Comprehension — reading fast and answering on time.
pre-toefl.fit1: You need a TOEFL score for university, a scholarship or a job.
pre-toefl.fit2: You have the basics and want to get used to the test format.
pre-toefl.fit3: You want timed practice, not just theory.
pre-toefl.next: After this program, you’re ready to sign up for an official TOEFL test.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.title: What people ask us most on WhatsApp.
faq.asideBody: Just message us. We reply during opening hours, {open}–{close} (WIB).

placement.q: Is the placement test free? What’s in it?
placement.a: It’s free, and you don’t have to enrol afterwards. It’s a relaxed chat with a teacher plus a few short questions, so we know which level fits best.

age.q: Which program is right for my child?
age.a: Roughly: kindergarteners go to Kindergarten, grades 1–3 to Standard, grades 4–6 to Primary, junior high to Elementary, high school and adults to Intermediate, and Pre-TOEFL is for test prep. But the placement test decides, not age.

duration.a: {months} months per level. A program with three levels takes about {total} months if you go all the way through.

fees.a: From {min} a month for Kindergarten up to {max} a month for Pre-TOEFL. The full breakdown is in Schedule & Fees.

schedule.a: We’re open {open}–{close} (WIB). Your exact schedule is set after the placement test, based on your level and the open slots.

online.a: Not at the moment. All classes are in person on Jalan Mawar. If your schedule is tricky, private classes can be arranged.

makeup.q: What if I miss a class?
makeup.a: Let us know before class starts and we’ll help you find a make-up class at the same level.

payment.a: Monthly, at the start of each month. Cash at the school or bank transfer.
